case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of both parents' rights, holding the juvenile court did not clearly err in finding that social services made the reasonable efforts required by statute to reunify the family before termination.
key_cases.relevance: Court-ordered service plans are measured by the statutory reasonable-efforts definition, and the sufficiency of those efforts is a finding reviewed for clear error.
key_cases.quote: This Court has recognized that juvenile court findings regarding whether the State made reasonable efforts to reunify children with parents is reviewed under the clearly erroneous standard.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding that concurrent planning as applied by the county — pursuing reunification and permanent placement at the same time under N.D.C.C. § 27-20-32.2 — did not violate the mother's due process rights or her right to a fair hearing.
key_cases.relevance: Approves concurrent planning: an agency may pursue a reunification service plan while simultaneously planning for permanency.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the concurrent planning as applied by Cass County did not violate S.D.'s due process rights

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding the juvenile court correctly applied the law and that clear and convincing evidence supported findings of deprivation, likely continuation of the causes of deprivation, resulting harm, and reasonable reunification efforts.
key_cases.relevance: The agency's court-ordered services were reviewed as part of the reasonable-efforts finding supporting termination.
key_cases.quote: These elements must be established by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that a state plan provide for 'reasonable efforts' to prevent removal and reunify families creates no right enforceable by beneficiaries under § 1983 or directly, leaving enforcement to the federal agency's plan-approval process.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable-efforts obligations attached to court-ordered services derive from a state-plan requirement not privately enforceable.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding the juvenile court did not clearly err in finding by clear and convincing evidence that deprivation was likely to continue, that the child would suffer harm absent termination, and that the State made the reasonable efforts required by N.D.C.C. § 27-20-32.2 by offering an array of services the mother largely declined.
key_cases.relevance: This is the direct North Dakota authority — reached indirectly in the brief through R.L.-P. — applying the statutory reasonable-efforts definition to a court-ordered service plan and reviewing the sufficiency of those services for clear error.
key_cases.quote: The State is not required to "exhaust every potential solution" before seeking termination of parental rights.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a twelve-month extension of a child's placement in the custody of county social services, holding the findings of continuing deprivation and of reasonable efforts to reunify and to maintain family connections were not clearly erroneous, and that the custodian did not abuse its authority by keeping the child with out-of-state relatives as the permanent plan.
key_cases.relevance: Sets out the statutory menu of dispositions under N.D.C.C. § 27-20-30 and the limits on extending a dispositional order, which is the mechanism by which court-ordered supervision and services continue year to year.
key_cases.quote: The custodian has an obligation and right to determine the nature of care, placement, and treatment of a child considering the child's best interests.

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The child must be released unless continued shelter care is found required; if no petition is filed within 30 days of protective custody the child must be released from shelter care (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 27-20.3-08(3), 27-20.3-10).

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the registered-mail, return-receipt-requested notice by the Indian child's parent, Indian custodian and tribe (15 days where notice goes to the United States secretary of the interior)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The first hearing in the proceeding may not be held until the ten days have run; on request of the parent, Indian custodian or tribe the court shall grant a continuance of up to twenty additional days (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-19.1-03(1)).

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Family case plan filed with juvenile court
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Commitment of the child to the human service zone by the juvenile court (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1) states only "within sixty days")
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1).
